name: Bildad
title: Shuhite – Job's Friend
summary: Bildad from Shuah was one of Job's three friends who came to comfort him in his suffering. He is known for his speeches where he defends God's justice and claims that Job's suffering must be due to sin. Bildad represents a traditional wisdom tradition that emphasizes the doctrine of retribution.

keyEvents.title: Visits Job in His Suffering
keyEvents.description: Bildad came together with Eliphaz and Zophar to show compassion and comfort Job after he was struck by disasters and illness. They sat silently with him for seven days and seven nights.

keyEvents.title: Bildad's First Speech
keyEvents.description: Bildad challenges Job and claims that God does not pervert justice. He suggests that Job's children died because of their sin, and urges Job to seek God and live righteously.

keyEvents.title: Bildad's Second Speech
keyEvents.description: Bildad describes the fate of the wicked in strong terms. He portrays how the wicked lose everything and are forgotten, indirectly suggesting that this applies to Job's situation.

keyEvents.title: Bildad's Third Speech
keyEvents.description: In his shortest speech, Bildad highlights God's majesty and human insignificance. He asks how a person can be righteous before God, emphasizing that even the moon and stars are not pure in God's eyes.

keyEvents.title: God rebukes Job's friends
keyEvents.description: God speaks to Eliphaz and includes Bildad in his rebuke. God says they have not spoken rightly about him as Job has, and commands them to offer burnt offerings while Job prays for them.
